retire: The bilateral partner COOLDOWN GATE: the refusal in planTrade (js/moves.js:398-401) and the filter in legal (js/moves.js:1299). Its function (stopping the same pair trading every turn) is replaced by COMMITMENT: a live deal occupies the matched flow it covers, `legal` offers a trade only where uncommitted matched flow remains, and planTrade refuses 'nothing left to trade' via its existing branch at :415-417. Nothing else reads the gate. The stamp it wrote stays (js/power.js:912 reads it). Without the commitment rule in place first, retiring the gate lets fifty AI nations sign a deal with every neighbour every turn — this replacement is load-bearing, not optional.

Immediate two-sided payout in resolveTrade (js/moves.js:443-444, `Game.earn(nid/target, gain*1e6)`): replaced by per-turn settlement of the deal. Depends on it: tests/trade.test.js:68-91 and :121-140 compute 'best single trade this turn' as min(matched, cap) x trade.gain — still true per turn of a deal, so they hold if trade.gain and the per-turn formula are unchanged; the AI scorer's `gain` (js/ai.js:318) which must stay per-turn.

The vestigial `Market.update(T(tune))` at js/moves.js:455 and its comment 'traded supply moves the prices'. It has not been able to move a price since M1.9 moved trade income to the treasury (js/actions.js:275-280; js/game.js:1620-1625): Market.update reads only Game.countyGdp/countyPop and market.demandShare (js/market.js:43, 63-64, 72), none of which a trade touches. Its only observable effects are `prev = prices` (js/market.js:70) which flattens the trend arrows in Market.html (:84-86), and a byte-identical recompute of perCap. It also costs a full 1,688-Area recompute per AI trade, up to fifty times a round. Nothing depends on it: `prev` is not in the fingerprint (tests/world-fixture.js:210 reads prices only) and no test reads it. The matching calls in the external/transit UI paths (js/actions.js:618, 675) are A2's surface and are NOT touched.

Actions.tradeFlows (js/actions.js:437-449): a pre-M11.1 duplicate with no caller — the only other reference to the name in the file is the definition itself; renderTradePreview reads Moves.plan(...).flows (:693-694). Delete.

The one-click preview/confirm panel as the player's trade surface (js/actions.js:690-751): becomes the negotiation panel (UI area's plan). The startTrade picker (:412-426), clickTrade (:428-434) and the panels.js button (js/panels.js:52) stay as the entry point.

steps.step: Extend, do not fork: keep the intent type 'trade'
steps.detail: planTrade takes optional terms {duration, autoRenew, price, volume} and defaults them from schema keys; every refusal at :393-411 stays verbatim (exists, self, adjacency, Recognition.canTrade) except the cooldown branch at :398-401, which goes. `gain` in the returned plan stays the per-turn figure so js/ai.js:316-319 needs no change. A new type name would break tests/moves.test.js:389 for nothing.

steps.step: Replace the cooldown gate with commitment, computed in Moves and never in Market
steps.detail: Add an 'uncommitted flows' helper in Moves that subtracts the volumes of live deals between the pair from tradeFlows' output; planTrade uses it and refuses through the existing 'Nothing to trade' branch at :415-417; legal offers a trade intent only where uncommitted total > 0. Market.nationSurplus is read, never adjusted — subtracting commitments inside Market would be a supply change and is the blocker in scopeCheck.

Remove the two Game.earn calls (:443-444) and the Market.update line (:455). Keep markTraded both sides (:445-446) so power.js:912 still sees the partner; keep Relations 'traded' both ways (:452-453), once per signing; create the Deal record with an id from the Deals module's counter; log kind 'trade' with `terms` carrying resource, volume, price, duration, autoRenew. Everything the plan quoted is what the deal carries — same contract as tests/moves.test.js:215-225.

steps.step: Settle inside the world tick, treasuries only
steps.detail: Deals.settle(tn) immediately after Game.tickTreasuries() and before Market.update(tn), inside the existing Game.batch (:1141) so N deals cost one emit. Per deal in ascending id: Game.earn each side vol x price/100 x trade.gain x 1e6, decrement remaining turns, queue expiries whose countdown is at 4/2/1 (schema keys) for the prompt. Drop deals whose party no longer exists, the way Pacts.tick does (js/world.js:1171-1173). Placement relative to phasePower is the tick area's call; wherever it sits it touches treasuries only.

steps.step: Register the new stateful module everywhere the save enumerates
steps.detail: assemble adds `deals: Deals.serialize()`; applyModel calls Deals.loadState(doc.deals) after Game.loadState (nation ids must exist) — a missing section restores to empty; STATEFUL_MODULES adds 'Deals'. tests/saves.test.js:277 hard-codes a local module map and will fail the moment 'Deals' is in STATEFUL_MODULES until that map lists it. No VERSION bump: validate (:127-138) refuses every existing save on a bump, and the section is additive.

`if (offerRenegotiation()) return true;` after the `won` check at :247 and before the crisis check at :250 — a dead or victorious player is not asked to renew anything. The A0 contract (:192-196) and fastForward (:270-272) already treat any `true` as a stop. Update the comment at :248-249.

steps.step: Delete the dead duplicate; leave A2's paths alone
steps.detail: Remove Actions.tradeFlows. Do not touch evalTransit, renderTransitPreview, renderExternalPreview or their cooldown reads and Market.update calls — the addendum assigns transit and the world-market route to A2.

Rewrite §Trade for standing agreements (terms, durations, expiry prompt, deal ledger), amend the nation-record line, add settlement to the turn order, strike the §12 stale note. Rule at CLAUDE.md:27-29: behaviour and DESIGN.md change together.

newTunables: deal.defaultDuration — the duration Moves.legal puts on a canonical trade intent (the AI's and the preview's starting term), one of 2/4/8/20; a placeholder, and the only new key this audit itself requires because legal cannot carry a literal. The deal-object area owns the rest (durations, countdown thresholds 4/2/1, offer expiry, auto-renew default); each must be a top-level two-space `'key': {` entry in js/tunables.js with label, group, doc over 20 characters and min/max/step, or tests/tunables.test.js:9-20 and :181-196 fail.
Nothing is retired from the schema: trade.cooldownTurns stays for the external and transit paths; trade.gain becomes the per-turn settlement rate under its existing doc.
scopeCheck: No step touches demand, supply or the price index. Demand: A1 reads market.demandShare only through Market.nationSurplus (js/market.js:104, 116) at signing; it writes nothing there. Supply: the index and nationSurplus both derive supply from live Area GDP (js/market.js:42-48, 63-64, 108-114), and money-only settlement credits treasuries (js/game.js:1626-1632), so GDP — and therefore supply — is untouched by construction; 'goods move' is deferred by addendum §4 row 1, and any temptation to make a buyer's volume arrive as GDP (Game.boostGdp, js/game.js:1611-1616) is that deferred item and is a BLOCKER. Price index: its only writer is the world tick at js/world.js:1216 (plus boot writers); A1 adds no writer, the deal stores the index value read at signing as its base price (spec v2 §1.5, §4.1; addendum §4 'the existing global index is the base price'), and a counter-offer edits the deal's own price field, never the index. Two near-misses named as blockers if attempted: (1) subtracting committed volume inside Market.nationSurplus — that is a supply-side change; commitment lives in Moves; (2) recomputing prices at signing or settlement. The resolveTrade `Market.update` at js/moves.js:455 is the question asked and the answer is: it is neither a price-index change to preserve nor the intended base-price behaviour — it is a vestige of the boostGdp era whose comment is stale. It cannot move the index because the inputs it reads (countyGdp, countyPop, demandShare — js/market.js:43, 63-64, 72) are unchanged by a trade; its whole effect is `prev = prices` (flat trend arrows, js/market.js:70, 84-86) and an identical perCap. New deal code never calls it; the line goes with the resolver it lives in; the world tick stays the sole writer; the external/transit copies at js/actions.js:618 and :675 are left for A2. Verify with the byte-identity test below.
determinism: Deal ids come from a module-level counter (`seq`) incremented in resolve only — the Relations pattern (js/relations.js:33-34, 109-116) — serialized and restored with the module (js/relations.js:207-213) so a loaded game continues the sequence; never from RNG, Date, or Math.random. `plan` stays pure and allocates nothing (tests/moves.test.js:26-40 contract). Deals are iterated in ascending id at settlement, expiry and in the ledger view; loadState rebuilds the Map from an array in id order so insertion order equals id order after a round trip. No RNG in signing, settlement, countdown or expiry; the AI's only draw stays the softmax at js/ai.js:619 (`rng.stream('ai')`), so the RNG call sequence is unchanged by A1. Settlement runs at one fixed point inside advanceTurn's batch (js/world.js:1141-1219), so the fingerprint (tests/world-fixture.js:187-214: prices, treasuries, turn order) reproduces; the saves tests at tests/saves.test.js:104-132 go through StateDoc (tests/saves.test.js:25-26), so registering Deals in assemble/applyModel is what keeps 'restored advances identically' true. Intents from `legal` are plain data with identical shape on every call (tests/ai.test.js:156 deepEqual against ranked[0].intent). The `tradeCooldown` stamp is written at signing only, not per settlement, so power.js reach and the transit-button block behave exactly as after a one-click deal today.
risks: No consent step exists in resolveTrade (js/moves.js:436-461): today an AI nation can impose a one-click trade on the player, harmless because both sides gain. A standing 20-turn deal imposed the same way is a different thing. The negotiation/AI area must decide whether AI-to-player intents in A1 become offers (A4's surface pulled forward minimally) or are held to the one-click equivalence (shortest duration, no auto-renew). AI-to-AI deals can stay immediate.

Standing accumulation changes shape in the Full game: today `traded` fires once per pair every trade.cooldownTurns (3); recorded once per signing, a 20-turn deal fires it once in five years. rel.magTraded feeds union odds (js/moves.js:833-836), release acceptance (rel.acceptFriend, :941) and coalition exemptions. Recording per settlement instead would multiply it. Neither is a tuning question A1 may answer; recording at signing and at renewal is the structural equivalent of today and should be stated in DESIGN.md as a thing the alpha watches.

The `tradeCooldown` key is shared by bilateral partners and transit routes (js/actions.js:489 disables transit through r.t when tradeCooldownLeft(nid, r.t) > 0). Stamping at signing reproduces today's quirk (a deal with Nevada blocks transit via Nevada for 3 turns); stamping per settlement would block it permanently. Write the stamp at signing only.

power.js reach (js/power.js:906-912) counts partners stamped within nation.historyWindow = 20 turns; a 20-turn deal that keeps settling stops counting toward Influence in its last turns unless renewed. Accepted approximation for A1 — switching reach to live deals changes Influence in the Full game and belongs with A3/A4, not here.

Ledger flood: ledger.cap is 4000 (js/tunables.js:524-526; the 5000 in js/ledger.js:84 is only the no-TUNE fallback). Logging every settlement (~60 deals x 60 turns) would push real news out of the cap and the save document. Log signing, expiry, renewal and countdown notices only; settlements belong in the deal ledger, not the event ledger.

Trade is not gated by Complexity (js/complexity.js:20-21; js/moves.js:1298-1300 has no flag), so A1 changes trade in the Full game as well as Economy mode. That is the alpha track's intent (addendum A1) but it must be said in DESIGN.md, and the whole suite — not only trade tests — is the bar.

A partner that dies mid-deal (merge, prune) must expire the deal deterministically in the tick, or Game.earn returns false silently (js/game.js:1627-1628) and the deal ledger shows a ghost. Copy Pacts.tick's drop-the-dead behaviour.

The tests/trade.test.js:68-91 'recovery path' assertion (coverable/deficit > 0.6) is arithmetic over helpers, not over resolveTrade; it survives only while one turn of a deal equals min(matched, cap) x trade.gain. If the deal-object area introduces any per-deal price factor, that test's premise and the scope rule both break together — which is the signal to stop.
tests: Signing a deal leaves Market.getPrices() byte-identical (JSON.stringify before/after), and so does settling it for six turns — the proof that A1 adds no price-index writer.

Settling one turn of a deal credits each treasury exactly what a one-click trade paid before A1: min(matchedValue, cap) x trade.gain x 1e6 — pinning the per-turn equivalence tests/trade.test.js:68-91 relies on.
Game.countyGdp for both parties is unchanged after signing and after settlement — money-only, no goods, no boostGdp.
Moves.plan({type:'trade', ...}) with and without terms changes nothing: Deals.count() and the fingerprint are equal before and after five calls.
Two worlds from the same seed that sign the same deals produce identical deal ids, identical settlement order and identical fingerprints after ten AI.round calls.
StateDoc.assemble -> applyModel round-trips active deals, open offers, countdowns and the id counter; 'a restored world advances identically to one that never saved' still passes with deals live.
Moves.legal offers no trade intent to a pair whose matched flow is fully committed, and offers one again the turn after the deal expires — the commitment rule replaces the cooldown.
Recognition.canTrade still refuses a deal between a parent and its unrecognised breakaway, in Full mode, and is permissive in Economy mode (D166).
A deal whose counterparty is removed from Game.nations mid-term is dropped by the next tick with no Game.earn call and no thrown error.
Every new schema key has label, group, doc over 20 characters and min/max/step, and the source scan in tests/tunables.test.js:181-196 still counts the same number of keys as SCHEMA.
A settled deal writes no ledger entry; signing, expiry and each 4/2/1 countdown notice write exactly one entry of kind 'trade', and every entry's kind is in Ledger.KINDS.
completeTurn returns true when a player's deal reaches a countdown threshold or expiry, and fastForward stops on that turn.
After signing, tradeCooldown[partner] equals the signing turn on both nations and is not rewritten by settlement, so gatherInfluence's partner count matches today's behaviour.
